chunk_findings.detail: When the refresh commit fails, the rollback is done with `git reset -q HEAD -- <paths>` followed by `git checkout -- <paths>`. That pair only restores *tracked* files. For a document that was newly generated by the refresh (a whole-file document is exactly something `export --update` can create when the file does not yet exist), the sequence is: `git add` stages the new `ROADMAP.md` (`add.ok` is true), the commit fails (e.g. `commit.gpgsign = true` with no key, or `user.email`/`user.name` unset — `--no-verify` does not bypass those), then `git reset HEAD -- ROADMAP.md` removes the index entry, leaving the file untracked, and `git checkout -- ROADMAP.md` fails with `error: pathspec 'ROADMAP.md' did not match any file(s) known to git`. The return value of both calls is ignored, so the freshly generated file is left on disk while `data["changed"] = []` and the `problems_note` falsely report that nothing was applied. The result contradicts the documented behaviour ("a refresh that fails … is reported and never fails the merge") because the worktree now contains an uncommitted generated document that the merge result claims does not exist, and it can contaminate a later merge/commit in that worktree. The rollback needs to remove newly created paths (e.g. `git rm --cached`/`clean`) rather than rely on `checkout`.

chunk_findings.detail:
The rollback after a failed `git commit` is:
```
W.git(wt.path, "reset", "-q", "HEAD", "--", *paths)
W.git(wt.path, "checkout", "--", *paths)
```
`reset HEAD -- p` only *unstages* `p` when `p` is a newly added file (it moves the index entry back to HEAD, where the path does not exist), and then `git checkout -- p` fails with `error: pathspec 'p' did not match any file(s) known to git`. The regenerated file is left sitting in the worktree as an untracked file, and `data["changed"] = []` / the summary still reporting it are now wrong.

Concrete input: a selected whole-file document that does not yet exist in the item branch's `HEAD` (e.g. a freshly configured `[export.ROADMAP].refresh = "merge"` whose document has not been committed), plus a commit that fails (very common in CI: missing `user.name`/`user.email`). `refresh_selected` returns the new path in `r.changed`, `git add` stages it, `git commit --no-verify -- <path>` fails, `reset` unstages it, `checkout` errors out, and the regenerated file remains uncommitted in `wt.path`. The merge then runs against a worktree that is no longer clean; given the `merge` path already refuses with `O.refused("worktree.merged", ..., dirty=...)`, this leftover untracked file can make `W.merge` refuse, so a refresh-commit error does fail the merge — contradicting the stated acceptance ("a refresh error does not fail the merge; it is reported"). It also means a rollback path claims `changed: []` while the worktree still holds the regenerated content.

chunk_findings.detail:
The loop that resolves the per-document specs is wrapped in a single `try` whose handler catches only `(ExportError, ValueError)` and then returns a single doc-less outcome (`DocOutcome("", action="failed", ...)`). Two problems follow from that structure, both contradicting this module's own stated contract ("a failure for one document ... is that document's outcome, never an exception: a refresh must not fail the operation that triggered it"):

1. Any exception of another type escapes `refresh_selected` entirely. `spec_for` resolves templates/registry entries and document paths, so a `KeyError` (unknown template/mode lookup), `OSError` (probing an unreadable target) or similar from one document's settings propagates out of the one entry point callers were told is total, and can fail the very merge/phase-close it is supposed to never fail — note that the log-loading path right below deliberately adds `OSError` to its handler and `_one` uses a blanket `except Exception`, so this loop is the one hole.
2. Even when the exception *is* caught, a problem in one selected document aborts the whole refresh, and the failure is attributed to `doc=""` rather than the offending document. Concretely: with `[export].documents = ["ROADMAP.md", "STATUS.md"]`, `ROADMAP.md` configured `refresh = merge` and `STATUS.md` carrying a bad/unsafe path that `spec_for` rejects, `ddflow merge` refreshes neither; `ROADMAP.md` is left stale and no outcome names `STATUS.md`. Worse, `spec_for` is called for *every* selected document before the `spec.refresh == trigger` filter, so a document that is not even part of this trigger's refresh (e.g. one with `refresh = off`) can block the documents that are, and the per-document "skipped/failed" reporting that the callers consume is never produced.

chunk_findings.detail: The rollback decides "the refresh created this file" solely from `HEAD:<rel>` existence. That proxy is wrong for a target document that already existed on disk before the refresh but is not committed at HEAD (untracked generated file, or a tracked file the user had deleted from the working tree — note the tests call `merge_item(..., allow_dirty=True)`). Concrete case: a repo containing an untracked, already-generated `ROADMAP.md` (e.g. the user ran `ddflow export` but never committed it), config `refresh = "merge"`, and a failing "refresh generated documents" commit (the exact case the new test manufactures). The refresh regenerates/stages `ROADMAP.md`, so it is in `paths`; the commit fails; `cat-file -e HEAD:ROADMAP.md` fails because the file was never committed; the `else` branch `unlink`s it. The pre-refresh state (a file that existed) is not restored — the file is deleted. The previous `git checkout -- *paths` left the working tree untouched in this situation. The fix should distinguish "not in HEAD" from "did not exist in the worktree before the refresh" (e.g. via the pre-refresh index/worktree state) rather than treating every non-HEAD path as created. Same class for a tracked-but-locally-deleted target: `checkout` resurrects the HEAD copy instead of leaving it absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle.py:1798 (`(wt.path / rel).unlink(missing_ok=True)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new rollback concludes "this document was created by the refresh" purely from `HEAD:<rel>` being absent, and deletes it with `unlink(missing_ok=True)`. But a selected document can be absent from `HEAD` for reasons that have nothing to do with this refresh: (a) the merge being processed introduced it (a source branch that added a configured, generated document — e.g. a branch that checked in a fresh `STATUS.md`), or (b) it is an untracked document that already existed in the worktree. In those cases the refresh merely overwrote/updated the file and the commit failed (the test uses a gpg failure, but any commit failure behaves the same); the `cat-file` probe fails, so the file is deleted from the worktree (and, because `git reset -q HEAD -- *paths` already ran, from the index) instead of being restored/left in place. Concretely: `documents = ["roadmap", "status"]`, `refresh = "merge"`, a source branch that adds `STATUS.md` is merged in, the docs commit fails → `HEAD:STATUS.md` does not exist, so `(wt.path / "STATUS.md").unlink()` removes the file the *merge* brought in, losing a document the merge was supposed to carry and leaving the retried/continued merge without it. The comment ("a document this refresh created") states an invariant the condition does not actually establish; the code needs to distinguish "created by this refresh" (e.g. via its own staged-added set / pre-refresh listing) from "absent from HEAD".
